themeVerdicts.explanation: Permanent publicly accessible covered food market in Barcelona; its present-site market structure was inaugurated in 1853, with the current metal roof added in 1914, and it remains operational.
Named public market established on its present site in 1845. Although substantially rebuilt, it remains a permanent operating covered market with public retail stalls.
Permanent covered public market opened in 1882 in Barcelona and still operating with food, household, and other retail stalls.
Named municipal covered market opened in 1888 and still operating as a public neighborhood market with everyday retail services.
Málaga’s permanent municipal market occupies a fixed historic complex; the present iron hall dates from the nineteenth century and remains an operating public food market.
Operating permanent covered public food market in London, with market activity documented on or near the present Southwark location for centuries and current public retail operations.
Individually named covered market in a fixed City of London complex, with market use on the site since the fourteenth century and current public shops and food businesses.
Fixed covered market complex with documented market origins in the seventeenth century and continuing public retail activity in its market buildings.
Public markets have occupied the Toronto site since 1803; the operating South Market building dates from 1845 and functions as a permanent covered food market.
Historic covered public market hall completed in 1826 and still operating with visitor-accessible food vendors and shops in a fixed Boston complex.
Permanent enclosed public market opened in 1893 and remains operational with independent food, produce, prepared-food, and merchandise vendors.
Permanent indoor municipal market opened in 1897 at its Budapest site, with operating stalls, published hours, and food and merchandise retail.
Named covered bazaar complex in Istanbul whose core construction began in 1455–56; it remains a fixed, publicly accessible retail complex with thousands of shops and regular hours.
Permanent covered public bazaar completed in 1664 and still operating with food, spice, sweet, and merchandise shops.
Named roofed market street in a fixed Kyoto arcade, with documented market authorization at the site in 1615 and approximately 130 operating food and goods shops.
Historic named bazaar in Cairo established in the fourteenth century and still operating as a contiguous covered public retail market area.
Fixed Jerusalem market complex established in 1887, now operating year-round with covered streets, public stalls, and shops selling food and other goods.
Historic covered municipal market opened in 1869 in Mumbai and still operating as a public retail market for food and household merchandise.
Permanent covered municipal market opened in 1874 and continuing as a public retail complex with food, clothing, and household shops.

Permanent named market complex officially opened in 1878 and still operates with covered halls and sheds, food and non-food retail, and public access. Its mixed open-air components do not trigger the exclusion for markets that are entirely open-air.

clueVerdicts.explanation: The clue uniquely matches Nishiki Market: its approximately 400-metre roofed arcade, roughly 130 shops, 1615 fish-selling authorization, 1984 floor, and 1993 canopy are all stated in the supplied evidence.
The covered core beginning in 1455–56, 61 covered streets, more than 4,000 shops, 30,700-square-metre area, and two bedestens directly identify Istanbul’s Grand Bazaar.
The 15 February 1897 opening, three-floor 10,000-square-metre steel hall, Zsolnay roof tiles, and ground-floor produce and spice stalls directly match the Great Market Hall.
The La Rambla entrance near the Liceu, 1217 history, 1853 inauguration, and 1914 metal roof uniquely identify Mercat de Sant Josep de la Boqueria.
The 1878 opening, seven-hectare scale, food halls and sheds, cemetery-site expansion, and 2003 solar panels directly match Queen Victoria Market.
